S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether the cause has been confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Manufacturers must submit each model's sample size, failure rate, and test results to the regulator and provide those per-model results to customers who buy that model. A result above 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale; the regulator will determine proportionate interim measures based on the evidence and risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For already-installed units that lack the function, manufacturers must complete a retrofit or provide an equivalent approved safety measure within 6 years of this standard taking effect. A regulator may approve a longer schedule for documented technical or access constraints, provided interim risk controls are in place.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect. A regulator may approve a narrowly tailored extension for documented technical constraints, with interim risk controls.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A model exceeding 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any year must be promptly reported to the regulator and triggers a prompt, documented regulator risk assessment. The regulator must determine whether a recall or other proportionate corrective action is necessary; a recall is mandatory when the assessment finds an unreasonable risk that cannot be adequately controlled by lesser measures.

document.section_notes: The final v12 keeps the 5% 55 °C test limit only as a regulator-review trigger, with no sales stop, so Northwind's flagship Hearth 10 (6.2%) is protected, while per-model results go to purchasers and regulators but not the public. S5 removes any mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 (the trigger only prompts a risk assessment, and recall is discretionary unless the regulator finds an unreasonable risk), which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). S3 (6-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month built-in suppression) sit inside the acceptable ranges and match each company's red lines; S1 sets 72-hour reporting for all thermal incidents, which benefits both companies given their unreported incidents.
